subject: Dracula ant
title: The Fastest Move in Nature Belongs to an Ant That Drinks Its Babies' Blood

scenes.text: Nothing on Earth moves faster than this ant's jaw.
Not a cheetah. Not a diving falcon. A tiny ant from the forest floor.
It presses its two jaws together until they bend like a bow. Then one slips past the other.
Zero to 200 miles an hour in 15 millionths of a second. About 5,000 snaps fit inside one blink.
Scientists needed a camera running at 480,000 frames a second just to see it happen.
And the name? The queens feed by piercing their own larvae and drinking their blood. The babies survive.

description:
The Dracula ant, Mystrium camillae, has the fastest animal movement ever recorded: its jaws snap at over 200 mph, going from zero to top speed in 0.000015 seconds, about 5,000 times faster than a blink.
Instead of a latch, it presses its mandibles together until they bend and one slips past the other, like a finger snap. Smithsonian researchers filmed it at 480,000 frames per second (Royal Society Open Science, 2018). The queens feed on the blood of their own larvae, which usually survive, hence the name.
What's the fastest animal you can think of? Comment below.
first_comment: Dracula ants live in Australia and tropical Southeast Asia and hunt under leaf litter. The snap beat the previous record, held by another ant, by about three times. Which animal record should we cover next?
